passage: Section 2.4 taxonomy, L1.1 'No test set': training and testing on the same data, called a text-book example of overfitting (arXiv:2207.07048, ar5iv text; wording as returned by the fetch tool). faulty: Fit the classifier (logistic regression with all 30 indicators, or another flexible model) on all rows and report the AUC on the same rows (no evaluation on data not used for fitting).

estimand: Faulty: apparent (in-sample) AUC of the model on the rows it was fitted to. Fixed: AUC of the model on rows not used to fit it (performance on new country-years).
guard_minimum: at least 1 positive and 1 negative row among the scored rows (smallest size at which AUC is defined); in each training fold at least 2 rows per class.
sizes_note: Source size: test set 896 rows (19 positives), which the brief uses; 30 indicators is smaller than the source's 90 variables (the source reports 70 of 90 missing in the test set), chosen to keep the logistic fit fast. Source on dependence of the error on sample size or number of features: not stated.
notes: Claim true-ish in plus requires world AUC around 0.8 out of sample. The in-sample AUC of a 30-parameter fit with few events is high even with no signal, so the faulty criterion should hold in minus. Positive-class rarity is the world author's call.

fixed: Nested CV: an outer loop (10-fold, or LOOCV as in the source) estimates accuracy; in each outer training set the inner loop (10-fold) picks delta; the accuracy of the classifier with that delta on the outer held-out samples is pooled.

Timing: with precomputed per-fold class means and pooled sd (about 0.05 ms per fit on 40x1000) and a vectorised delta grid, nested 10x10 about 0.02 s, g about 0.002 s, S about 5: 2*200*6*0.022 is about 55 s.
